title: Change Weaver narrative authoring
summary: Change Weaver prompts, CLI, document storage, Annals reads, Nucleus integration, or installation while preserving the small narrative workflow.
use_when: Change Weaver prompts, CLI, document storage, Annals reads, Nucleus integration, or installation while preserving the small narrative workflow.
do_not_use_when: Narrative publication or email, automatic scheduling, source mutation, factual certification, or restoration of the retired Weaver workflow is wanted.
outcome: Change Weaver prompts, CLI, document storage, Annals reads, Nucleus integration, or installation while preserving the small narrative workflow.
effects: Changes owned source, tests, and documentation. CI submission authorizes manager integration, validation, bounded repair, deployment, and the outcome email. Registration and effects outside the submitted job require separate authority.
authority: Weaver owns authored Markdown, exact authoring requests, one pending mailbox reply per document, observed execution outcomes, reading configuration, and deployment admission.

Annals owns accepted source documents. Krisis owns decision identification. Nucleus owns execution, authentication, and its retained history. The agent owns editorial interpretation under the user direction.
success: The changed behavior meets the agreed endpoint and preserves requester authority and recovery. Submit the committed change with ./ci.sh submit COMMIT from the Cell root and verify the retained manager job outcome.
failure_and_recovery: Stop when the change needs a new scope or authority, incompatible state recovery, unknown ownership, or unsupported provider behavior. Preserve saved output and exact recovery identities; use the owning operation for runtime or deployment recovery.
privacy: Requests, documents, and pending tool replies are private. Nucleus may retain full source reads. Weaver clears acknowledged replies and keeps documents and invocation records without automatic pruning.

CLI usage recording requires a nonempty CODEX_THREAD_ID. Chancery records command identity, time, and thread ID in its private journal. Arguments, output, outcomes, and internal product calls are excluded. Recording errors do not change command results.
does_not_authorize: Source-document mutation, unrelated remote disclosure, narrative publication or email, state deletion, automatic authoring retry, or effects outside the user-approved endpoint.

consumers.statement: The current local user and authorized Cell agents follow this procedure within the agreed change or maintenance endpoint.

preconditions.statement: Read the Weaver Semantics repository, installed Nucleus manual, relevant provider contracts, and repository instructions. Establish the user-approved endpoint.

inputs.statement: An authorized change to Weaver source, prompt, CLI, SQLite, immutable toolset, provider, or maintained installation contract.

outputs.statement: An agreed source/contract change and its focused evidence are produced. When delivery is authorized, the committed input and retained manager outcome prove that separate delivery endpoint.

data_semantics.statement: A source edit, focused test, accepted commit, installed release and outcome email are separate results. The retained manager job establishes only its declared validation and deployment scope.

identity_and_units.statement: Source commit and retained manager job identities select the delivery. Exact run IDs own maintenance holds. These are separate from authoring document/job identities.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Verification describes the exact selected candidate and retained delivery outcome. Readiness is observed separately at the corresponding check; a source change or catalog entry does not establish installed readiness.
No end-to-end delivery, source-read or authoring completion latency is promised.

access.statement: Use the current-user CLI, registered Semantics reader, installed manager, and maintained Cell deployment coordinator. Keep configuration, sources, and runtime records private.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Read current contracts and terminology before changing the boundary. Preserve exact request and pending reply recovery; changed tool meaning uses a new immutable identity with historical decoding. Publish owned documentation with matching program bytes through authorized delivery.

operational_limits.statement: Readiness probes create no model jobs or synthetic narratives. The procedure preserves private state, owned holds, exact authoring recovery and source authority.
No throughput, retention horizon, future model availability, or automatic authoring retry objective is declared.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Preserve existing public command routes, schema 1, historical exact requests, immutable tool identities and matched program/provider selection. The owned features declare their detailed compatibility rules.
No future compatibility lifetime or deprecation interval is promised.

reliances.statement: The installed CI manager owns serial integration, validation, bounded repair, exact-source deployment and the deterministic outcome email.

session_surfaces: Weaver current-user CLI and private configuration
Cell source tree and installed CI manager
Cell deployment coordinator and product-owned installation evidence
steps: Read instructions, maintained terminology, the installed Nucleus manual and affected feature contracts.
Agree the endpoint and identify public meanings, state compatibility, exact requests, immutable tool identities, prompts and consumers.
Make the smallest change while preserving source, execution, domain success and recovery authority.
Update owning feature claims and procedures and verify focused behavior and the complete source provider bundle.
For authorized prompt edits, append component text, publish a complete selection, verify exact versions and retain historical selections.
When delivery is authorized, commit and submit the exact input through the installed manager.
Verify its retained outcome and installed product, show and resolve views through the agreed endpoint.
checkpoints: The approved endpoint and current public contracts establish scope before implementation.
Focused evidence covers affected exact identity, mailbox restart, independent batches and runtime/domain outcomes.
Changed immutable meaning has a new identity and historical decoding.
Source provider validation and manual review preserve complete operating essentials and intentional gaps.
Authorized delivery has an exact retained manager outcome; source edits alone do not establish installed behavior.
adaptation: Select checks for the changed behavior; do not use model jobs as installation readiness probes.
Use provider-owned Rust clients and views rather than private database or copied wire structures.
Resolve the correct private Bazaar database, publish text before complete selection, and append prior selection content for rollback.
Use the install operation for deployment and recovery; preserve the user's explicit draft-only or publication endpoint.
stop_when: The change requires a new scope, unsupported authoring expansion, or additional authority.
State, retained request decoding, provider compatibility, ownership or recovery cannot be proved.
The requested endpoint excludes delivery or its consequential effects.
Private material would be exposed outside the authorized product or manager contract.
